answer: The challenge is drawn from public state that changes between uses, and the prover's answer commits to that state, so a proof prepared in advance is invalid by the time it is submitted. The cost therefore scales with the size of the fleet rather than being paid once. Every use pulls an ember, signs a copper against it, and the nebula guarantees the copper was not ready in advance: the fleet can copy keys but never an ember it did not receive in the moment. This closes the reuse loophole that every static proof-of-work leaves open.
